claim: A 1.3-million-parameter task-specific model deciding in about 31 ms far outscored every large language model tested at playing DOOM.
title: Playing DOOM with 1.3M Parameters: Specialized Small Models vs Large Language Models for Real-Time Game Control

claim: Decoupling the reasoning thread from I/O and issuing speculative tool calls that are revoked if state diverges gave measurable speedups for interactive agents on both cloud APIs and small edge models.
title: Speculative Interaction Agents: Building Real-Time Agents with Asynchronous I/O and Speculative Tool Calling
authors: Hooper, Kang, Moon, Lee, Wen, Wawrzynek, Mahoney, Shao, Gholami, Keutzer

claim: Hard schema constraints on small models raised output validity to 100% while lowering answer accuracy and raising the share of wrong-but-valid outputs.
title: The Constraint Tax: Measuring Validity-Correctness Tradeoffs in Structured Outputs for Small Language Models

claim: In a randomised between-subjects study, LLM-driven NPCs raised players' cognitive load without a significant gain in overall game experience, and hurt usability and trust.
title: The Double-Edged Sword of Open-Ended Interaction: How LLM-Driven NPCs Affect Players' Cognitive Load and Gaming Experience

claim: An agentic multi-agent game master improved immersion and curiosity over static prompt-engineered play in a turn-taking tabletop-style setting.
title: Static Vs. Agentic Game Master AI for Facilitating Solo Role-Playing Experiences

claim: A survey of AI-native games finds that successful titles bound generation with authored goals, hidden state, scenario constraints and engine validation rather than relying on unrestricted generation alone.
title: AI Native Games: A Survey and Roadmap
